problems: The new E26 and E25 results strengthen the FOXA1 and GATA3 allele-binding predictions with models specific to those TFs, but both remain in-vitro predictions and do not demonstrate greater occupancy by the T allele in cells.

E27 strengthens the gene–breast cancer link for TOX3; it does not connect this variant or cCRE to TOX3 regulation. E06's contact is from other biosamples, and the element has no reported eQTL or CRISPR perturbation link.

TF expression and nearby ChIP-seq summits support presence at the site, but the cCRE is called inactive in MCF-7 by E05. This leaves the functional relevance of the proposed element in the case's expression context unresolved.
The T allele's breast-cancer association is supported, but none of the cited evidence establishes that any one of the proposed TFs mediates the association through TOX3.

checks.why: Clarifies the model coverage and allele-specific QBiC prediction for the leading GATA3 binding hypothesis.
Clarifies the model coverage and allele-specific QBiC prediction for the competing FOXA1 binding hypothesis.
Tests whether independent gene-disease evidence strengthens TOX3 as the target gene, which is the shared weak link across the chains.

critique.next_experiment: Test allele-specific occupancy in MCF-7 for GATA3 and FOXA1, then use endogenous allele editing or element perturbation with TOX3 expression readout to establish whether the site is functional and identify the relevant TF.

games.reason: Both chains share the same enhancer inactivity, candidate TOX3 link, and breast-cancer association, so those do not separate them. GATA3 is better supported because its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts greater binding to T, consistent with the GATA-family predictions, and it has a ChIP-seq summit 8 bp from the variant in MCF-7. MSX2 also has a nearby summit and the family screen’s aggregate prediction favors T, but the screened models disagree on direction and the best model is LHX8 rather than MSX2. Neither chain establishes regulation of TOX3 or a TF-mediated disease mechanism.

GATA3 is better supported because it has an explicitly mapped own QBiC-SELEX model predicting stronger binding to T than C (E25), alongside MCF-7 expression and a ChIP-seq summit 8 bp from the variant (E14). MSX2 has nearby MCF-7 ChIP-seq and expression, but its family-screen result uses an LHX8 model, reports model disagreement on direction, and does not provide an MSX2-specific model result (E13). The element’s MCF-7 inactivity and the indirect TOX3 link limit both chains equally.
